question.text: The Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III AIF) has a corpus of INR 200 crore across 20,00,000 units, giving a gross NAV of Rs. 1,000. An illiquid position (INR 20 crore book value) is identified as stressed and is SIDE-POCKETED. After side-pocketing, what is the main-scheme NAV and the side-pocket NAV per unit?

answer.text: Main NAV Rs. 1,000; side-pocket NAV Rs. 0 (written off)
Main NAV Rs. 900; side-pocket NAV Rs. 100 per unit (each unitholder's proportional share of the INR 20 cr segregated at its last marked value)
Main NAV Rs. 800; side-pocket NAV Rs. 200
Main NAV Rs. 1,000; side-pocket NAV Rs. 1,000 (duplicate units)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Side-pocket segregates an illiquid asset into a separate sub-scheme. INR 20 cr (illiquid) / 20,00,000 units = Rs. 100 per unit gets isolated in the side-pocket. The remaining INR 180 cr / 20,00,000 units = Rs. 900 per unit is the main-scheme NAV. Every existing unitholder gets 1 main unit (Rs. 900) + 1 side-pocket unit (Rs. 100) per original unit. **The Trap:** Option A wrongly writes off the asset at segregation (side-pocket holds it at last marked value, not zero). Option C miscalculates the split. Option D doubles units — wrong. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D (Cat I/II) has drawdown-waterfall, rare side-pocketing. XIX-C / XIX-E test side-pocket mechanics for Cat III. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When you side-pocket, new subscriptions post-segregation get NO side-pocket exposure — only main-scheme. Document this in the PPM and confirmations so new investors are not aggrieved by the legacy illiquid sleeve.
